theme_measure_sec <- function() {
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 10, base_family = "sans") +
    ggplot2::theme(
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),

## Scope

This vignette uses `sec_copolymer`, a synthetic dataset with one supplied
styrene fraction and one supplied molecular-weight value per sample. The
per-slice UV and RI signals can be used to calculate a relative detector
response profile. They do not, by themselves, give a mass fraction.

`step_sec_composition()` requires four detector-response coefficients
calibrated from pure-component standards for the selected input basis. The
example dataset does not include those calibration results, so the composition
calculation below is shown as a template rather than filled with assumed
coefficients.

## Sample-level composition values

```{r setup}
library(measure)
library(measure.sec)
library(recipes)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
```

```{r data}
data(sec_copolymer, package = "measure.sec")

sample_composition <- sec_copolymer |>
  distinct(sample_id, styrene_fraction) |>
  mutate(acrylate_fraction = 1 - styrene_fraction) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(styrene_fraction, acrylate_fraction),
    names_to = "component",
    values_to = "fraction"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    component = recode(
      component,
      styrene_fraction = "Styrene",
      acrylate_fraction = "Acrylate"
    )
  )

sample_composition
```

The bars use the sample-level fraction fields supplied with the synthetic
dataset. They do not show slice-level composition recovered from the detector
signals.

```{r sample-composition, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Sample-level styrene and acrylate fractions supplied with the synthetic dataset. Acrylate is shown as the complement of the supplied styrene fraction.", fig.alt = "Stacked bar chart of six synthetic samples, with styrene and acrylate fractions totaling 100 percent in each bar. Copoly-20S, Copoly-40S, Copoly-60S, and Copoly-80S contain 20, 40, 60, and 80 percent styrene; PA-Homo contains 0 percent and PS-Homo contains 100 percent."}
ggplot(
  sample_composition,
  aes(x = sample_id, y = fraction, fill = component)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, colour = "white") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(),
    limits = c(0, 1),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Styrene = "#A23B72", Acrylate = "#2E86AB")) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Supplied sample-level fraction",
    fill = "Component"
  ) +
  theme_measure_sec() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

## UV/RI response profiles

`step_sec_uv_ri_ratio()` retains a relative UV-to-RI response curve. Baseline
correction is applied before calculating the ratio. The step sets ratios to
`NA` where the RI signal is below its configured signal threshold; the plot
keeps those gaps instead of connecting across them.

```{r ratio-workflow}
copolymer_samples <- sec_copolymer |>
  filter(startsWith(sample_id, "Copoly"))

ratio_recipe <- recipe(
  ri_signal + uv_254_signal + elution_time ~ sample_id,
  data = copolymer_samples
) |>
  update_role(sample_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_measure_input_long(
    ri_signal,
    location = vars(elution_time),
    col_name = "ri"
  ) |>
  step_measure_input_long(
    uv_254_signal,
    location = vars(elution_time),
    col_name = "uv"
  ) |>
  step_sec_baseline(measures = c("ri", "uv")) |>
  step_sec_uv_ri_ratio(
    uv_col = "uv",
    ri_col = "ri",
    smooth = TRUE
  )

ratio_results <- prep(ratio_recipe) |>
  bake(new_data = NULL)

sample_fractions <- copolymer_samples |>
  distinct(sample_id, styrene_fraction)

ratio_data <- ratio_results |>
  select(sample_id, uv_ri_ratio) |>
  unnest(uv_ri_ratio) |>
  left_join(sample_fractions, by = "sample_id") |>
  group_by(sample_id) |>
  mutate(segment = cumsum(is.na(value))) |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  ungroup()

head(ratio_data)
```

```{r ratio-profiles, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Baseline-corrected UV-to-RI detector-response ratios calculated by `step_sec_uv_ri_ratio()` for the four synthetic copolymer samples. The ratio is not calibrated to a mass fraction.", fig.alt = "Line chart of elution time in minutes versus UV 254 nm to RI detector-response ratio for the synthetic samples Copoly-20S, Copoly-40S, Copoly-60S, and Copoly-80S. Each sample has its own colored curve; low-signal regions are omitted and remain visible as gaps. The curves describe relative detector response, not mass fraction."}
ggplot(
  ratio_data,
  aes(
    x = location,
    y = value,
    colour = sample_id,
    group = interaction(sample_id, segment)
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.9) +
  labs(
    x = "Elution time (min)",
    y = "UV 254 nm / RI detector-response ratio",
    colour = "Sample"
  ) +
  theme_measure_sec()
```

The ratio uses the native detector-response basis. Its magnitude depends on the
detector channels and their calibration. A changing profile can be investigated
as possible compositional variation, but interpreting it as composition
requires response calibration and suitable detector alignment.

## Calculating component mass fractions

Use `step_sec_composition()` after measuring the four response coefficients
from pure-component standards on the same instrument and with the same signal
basis. The code below leaves those measured values as inputs because they are
not supplied by `sec_copolymer`.

```{r composition-template, eval=FALSE}
composition_recipe <- recipe(
  ri_signal + uv_254_signal + elution_time ~ sample_id,
  data = copolymer_samples
) |>
  update_role(sample_id, new_role = "id") |>
  step_measure_input_long(
    ri_signal,
    location = vars(elution_time),
    col_name = "ri"
  ) |>
  step_measure_input_long(
    uv_254_signal,
    location = vars(elution_time),
    col_name = "uv"
  ) |>
  step_sec_baseline(measures = c("ri", "uv")) |>
  step_sec_composition(
    uv_col = "uv",
    ri_col = "ri",
    component_a_uv = styrene_uv_response,
    component_a_ri = styrene_ri_response,
    component_b_uv = acrylate_uv_response,
    component_b_ri = acrylate_ri_response,
    output_col = "styrene_fraction"
  )
```

The response coefficients must describe measured detector outputs per
concentration for the selected basis. Literature extinction coefficients or
`dn/dc` values alone do not supply these instrument-specific coefficients.

The `mw` column in `sec_copolymer` is a supplied sample-level value, repeated
across the elution-time rows. It is not a calibrated per-slice molecular-weight
curve, so these examples do not plot within-sample composition against MW.
